_doc: Slices of the agent-time donut (view command). 'leaf' lists timeline categories (the part before ':' counts, so 'mcp' covers every 'mcp:<server>'). Every second of autonomous time ends in exactly one leaf category; waits on subagents and background tasks are first resolved to what the child or the background command was doing. Slices under merge_below_pct of agent time fold into 'other' (unknown_wait stays visible above keep_unknown_above_pct). finding_segments puts a ranked finding into a slice: a segment id, a list (first visible wins), '@cmd' (classify the finding's example command) or null (not shown). Unlisted stack rules use '@cmd'. command_wrappers are regexes stripped from the start of each command part before naming it; noise_commands never name a command when a more specific part exists. deploy_parts: a part matching one of these (after unwrapping) is a deploy; it names the command and moves its time to the 'deploy' leaf unless the whole command was classed build/test/install/media (the deploy usually waits for a rollout, the health checks around it are quick). segment_rules: actions for a whole slice, shown when the slice has at least min_pct of agent time and min_runs runs; {n} = runs of all its items, {p50} = median of its top item, {total} = the slice's time, {what} = the top item's command; saving = saving_fraction x the slice's time (omit it when there is no honest estimate).

segment_rules.title: Deploy once per batch of fixes, not after every fix
segment_rules.why: Every deploy blocks the agent for the whole build and rollout ({p50} each here), however small the change.
segment_rules.evidence: {n} deploys in the window, median {p50}, {total} of agent time ({what})
segment_rules.assumption: half of the deploys could have waited for the next fix; every deploy takes about the median
segment_rules.before: fix A, deploy ({p50}); fix B, deploy ({p50})
segment_rules.after: fix A, fix B, tests, then one deploy; deploy at once only for a hotfix

segment_rules.title: Run the deploy in the background; check its build cache and queue
segment_rules.why: While the deploy builds and rolls out ({p50} median) the agent only waits. A background run reports its end, so the agent can prepare the next change; a deploy that rebuilds everything each time usually misses a build cache or waits in a queue.
segment_rules.assumption: no time estimate: the gain depends on how much other work is ready while the deploy runs
segment_rules.before: {what} in the foreground, the agent waits {p50}
segment_rules.after: {what} with run_in_background, continue; read the build log for uncached or unused build steps
